Let $N=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)$ be an NFA with epsilon-moves, and let
$S\subseteq Q$.

The **epsilon-closure** of $S$, written $\operatorname{ECl}(S)$, is the set of
all states $q\in Q$ for which there exist a state $s\in S$ and a finite
sequence of states
$$ s=r_0,r_1,\dots,r_n=q $$
such that $r_{i+1}\in\delta(r_i,\varepsilon)$ for every $0\le i<n$.

Equivalently, $\operatorname{ECl}(S)$ is the least subset $T\subseteq Q$ with
$S\subseteq T$ and $\delta(t,\varepsilon)\subseteq T$ for every $t\in T$.

For a single state $q\in Q$ we abbreviate
$$ \operatorname{ECl}(q):=\operatorname{ECl}(\{q\}). $$

Step 1.1 gives $\operatorname{ECl}(S)\subseteq\operatorname{ECl}(\operatorname{ECl}(S))$. For the reverse inclusion, let $q\in\operatorname{ECl}(\operatorname{ECl}(S))$. By [L1], there is an $\varepsilon$-chain from some $r\in\operatorname{ECl}(S)$ to $q$, and again by [L1] there is an $\varepsilon$-chain from some $s\in S$ to $r$. Concatenating the two finite chains gives an $\varepsilon$-chain from $s$ to $q$, so $q\in\operatorname{ECl}(S)$. Therefore $\operatorname{ECl}(\operatorname{ECl}(S))=\operatorname{ECl}(S)$.

$$ D_N=(\mathcal P(Q),\Sigma,\mu,S_0,G), $$

$$ \widehat\delta:\mathcal P(Q)\times\Sigma^*\to\mathcal P(Q) $$

$$ \widehat\delta(S,\varepsilon):=\operatorname{ECl}(S) $$

$$ \widehat\delta(S,wa):=\operatorname{ECl}\!\Bigl(\bigcup_{q\in\widehat\delta(S,w)}\delta(q,a)\Bigr) $$

$a\in\Sigma$.

For a single state $q\in Q$ we abbreviate
$$ \widehat\delta(q,w):=\widehat\delta(\{q\},w). $$

Thus $\widehat\delta(S,w)$ is the set of states that can be reached by starting
in some state of $S$, taking any number of $\varepsilon$-moves before and
